title.value: Trade-off between accuracy and fairness of data-driven building and indoor environment models: A comparative study of pre-processing methods
title.justification: The title directly refers to exploring the balance between accuracy and fairness in data-driven models for buildings, indicating a focus on improving these models' performance in the building environment sector.
title.quote: Trade-off between accuracy and fairness of data-driven building and indoor environment models: A comparative study of pre-processing methods

extractions.description: This paper investigates the trade-offs between accuracy and fairness in data-driven predictive models for buildings and indoor environments. It introduces fairness-aware prediction methods, evaluates different pre-processing techniques on the predictive fairness and accuracy of models, particularly in lighting status prediction scenarios, and discusses the implications for smart home energy management and associated systems.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on developing fair and accurate predictive models related to building energy consumption and smart home energy management systems, which directly relates to improving energy efficiency and reducing energy usage in buildings, crucial aspects of Climate Change Mitigation.
climate_change_is_central.quote: As smart home energy management systems (HEMS) and sensors are rapidly gaining popularity, an abundance of information (indoor temperature, humidity, motion status, CO2 concentration, and energy consumption, etc.) could be dynamically collected from buildings.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus on improving fairness and accuracy in data-driven predictive models for building energy consumption clearly aligns it with Climate Change Mitigation efforts aimed at enhancing energy efficiency in buildings.
primary_category.quote: These models could be further integrated into a model predictive controller (MPC) that can predefine optimal control signals based on users’ demand, and control relevant devices via HEMS to achieve cost/energy saving, or peak shifting.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not directly address any other primary climate change categories beyond its focus on energy efficiency in buildings.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study of improving predictive models that can help optimize energy usage and control in building settings directly ties into efforts to increase energy efficiency in buildings, which is a significant aspect of Climate Change Mitigation.
primary_sub_category.quote: Existing building and indoor environment models were mostly evaluated or validated by accuracy measures to show the perfor- mance gap that infers the differences between predicted values and measured/simulated values.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary sub-categories addressed in this paper as it is specifically focused on energy efficiency within buildings.

applications.value: Improving predictive models for energy efficiency in buildings
applications.justification: The paper discusses data-driven models for building energy consumption, indoor temperature, and HVAC systems which are crucial for optimizing energy use and reducing greenhouse gases in building operations.
applications.quote: These models could be further integrated into a model predictive controller (MPC) that can predefine optimal control signals based on users’ demand, and control relevant devices via HEMS to achieve cost/energy saving, or peak shifting.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing Climate Change Mitigation category for Energy Efficiency in Buildings sufficiently covers the scope of the paper.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Energy Efficiency in Buildings is an appropriate sub-category for the paper's content, with no need for a new sub-category.
